description: Start, talk to, and remove other agents that run next to you (on the same daemon). Two ways to start one. op new: write a NEW definition folder at path (a copy of the template from, then your files / llm / tools / tools_rm applied to it; or the whole folder from files only), then start it; the folder stays and can be started again later with op add. op add: start an EXISTING definition def as it is; llm / tools / tools_rm change only this child (kept in its own stack), the definition is not copied or changed. A child does NOT inherit your brain or tools; set llm / tools if you want them. ws is the child's workspace: relative to yours, or absolute; default is your own workspace (shared files). op say: send a child a message and return at once. op ask: send a message and wait for its answer. op rm: remove a child. op ls: the daemon table, your children and your max. say / ask / rm only work on children you started yourself. You may have at most max_children children at once (default 4); over that, new / add fail with ChildSlotMissing and nothing is started: rm one first. The daemon's judge may also refuse (AddRejected ... SlotMissing) when the whole daemon is full.

name.description: the child's name (new, add, say, ask, rm); letters, digits, _ and -

def.description: add: the existing definition folder, relative to your workspace or absolute; it must declare aos-agent in interfaces.json

path.description: new: where to write the new definition folder, relative to your workspace (it must stay inside it and must not exist yet)

from.description: new: the template folder to copy, relative to your workspace or absolute (e.g. the absolute path of proto8/demo/agent-fsm); leave it out to write the whole definition with files

files.description: new: files to write into the new definition, {relative path: full text}, e.g. {"system.txt": "You are a careful reviewer."} (agent-fsm keeps its system prompt in system.txt)

llm.description: new, add: brain settings, e.g. {"endpoint": "fake"} (agent-fsm) or {"model": "haiku"} (eca); new writes them into the definition's llm file, add into the child's own copy; default is what the definition says

tools.description: new, add: tools to give it (replaces one with the same name)

path.description: tool folder, relative to your workspace or absolute

tools_rm.description: new, add: names of tools to take away from it

ws.description: new, add: its workspace, relative to yours or absolute; created if missing; default is your own workspace

limits.description: new, add: resource limits for it, e.g. {"mem_mb": 512, "cpu_s": 600}; keys mem_mb, cpu_s, procs, file_mb, files (positive integers), user (string); default is what its definition declares

timeout_s.description: ask: seconds to wait for the answer; default 600, at most 1700
